A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SIMPLER and contain readable main texts and complete supplementary material. Equations, tables, figures and relocated content can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, classification and time-series experiments, alongside similarity analyses, ablations and linear-probing results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds LayerDrop comparisons, block-selection controls, SoftCon analysis, SAR classification and Jetson measurements.

M1.justification: The similarity computation, cutoff criterion and pruning algorithm remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm S1. Appendix G.1 adds an optional SIMPLER+LayerDrop variant that applies structured layer dropout during fine-tuning of the retained stack, providing a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from optical multispectral and RGB imagery to Sentinel-1 SAR through BigEarthNet-S1 classification with TerraMind-Large (Appendix G.3). This adds a distinct sensing modality. The SoftCon and Jetson experiments reuse MADOS rather than expanding dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table S14 adds LayerDrop at 50% expected depth and SIMPLER+LayerDrop comparisons on MADOS for Prithvi-300M and TerraMind-Large/Tiny. Table S16 adds random-k and last-k selection controls. Existing comparator sets remain intact; LayerDrop was previously discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 50%-expected-depth LayerDrop configurations, matched five-block selection controls, a two-block TerraMind SAR configuration, and measurements on Jetson Orin 32. Existing training hyperparameters and evaluation settings are retained. SoftCon uses the established 500-sample CKA protocol.

E4.justification: The matched-depth ablation directly tests whether retaining early pretrained blocks matters beyond reducing depth (Table S16). SoftCon adds an applicability analysis for contrastive pretraining (Figure S6), and the Jetson study checks hardware transfer of efficiency gains. Table S13 redisplays the existing Figure 3 cost analysis.

E5.justification: Existing five-seed protocols and mean-plus-standard-deviation results remain unchanged. Reporting becomes less consistent in the additions: LayerDrop Table S14 provides point estimates without uncertainty, while Table S17 reports variability only for training time. These omissions do not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–7 and S1–S12 retain their values. New results include LayerDrop comparisons, first/random/last-block mIoU of 62.8/49.7/41.8, SAR mAP of 61.1 versus 65.8 for the baseline, and Jetson inference times of 2.31 versus 8.97 seconds (Tables S14–S17). SoftCon adds a non-stabilizing similarity pattern. These are additional results under their respective settings.

T1.justification: The cutoff optimization, consecutive-row variability definition, Algorithm S1 and similarity-metric equations S1–S3 are unchanged. The revised applicability discussion supplies empirical qualifications rather than new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The conclusion substantially narrows applicability: v1 claims generalization to MAE and contrastive pretraining, whereas v2 restricts the supported claim to MAE-style models and leaves non-stabilizing contrastive models to future work. It also explicitly adds SAR to validated modalities. The central compression contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C now treats non-stabilizing contrastive models as an applicability boundary. New interpretations attribute gains to transferable early blocks and contextualize weak MADOS adaptation results as dataset-specific. Some additions overreach: Table S14 shows LayerDrop increasing TerraMind training time, and the random-k/last-k means lie outside the quoted 44.1–46.7 from-scratch range.

D1.justification: Appendix F.5 explicitly documents CPU/RAM pre-analysis cost and its exclusion from reported GPU costs, tabulating the existing Figure 3 measurements. v2 also identifies the Jetson deployment hardware. Existing hyperparameter tables and the code-access URL remain unchanged; Appendix G explicitly defers fuller experimental documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gromov et al. on deep-layer redundancy, Wanyan et al. for SoftCon, and Thoreau et al. on geospatial adaptation, with targeted contextual discussion. Earlier references are retained. LayerDrop and DepGraph were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain intact. v2 locally revises the discussion and conclusion, expands Appendix C into subsections, adds F.5 and G, standardizes supplementary references, and replaces the supplementary title page's missing-affiliation placeholder.

P2.justification: v2 adds the SoftCon heatmap and Tables S13–S17 while retaining existing visual designs. Table S13 presents Figure 3 data in tabular form; the other new tables display added experiments. Earlier segmentation figures S6–S9 become S7–S10. Front matter and page breaks change, including a nearly empty page 29.

improvement.justification: The matched-depth controls strengthen the layer-selection evidence, SAR and Jetson measurements substantiate broader practical applicability, and the SoftCon analysis corrects v1's overbroad contrastive-learning claim. Benefits are tempered by abbreviated experimental documentation, incomplete uncertainty reporting, and the table/prose inconsistencies in G.1–G.2. Overall, the added validation and clearer scope provide a limited net improvement.
